design: Before the set was built, the changes were read blind in three rounds of test scenes, fourteen pictures, one reader each, with the screen's own prompt (`vision/design_tests_v011.md`). The swing's motion arcs read ("motion lines show she is moving"), the hat flew with the gust ("blowing from left to right and has carried away a red baseball cap and a few green and brown leaves"), the seesaw's bigger child sat on the low end, and the play bow faced a person ("facing the kite child as if it wants to play"). The first round sent back four more changes: a pointer at the storm whose hand ended at the corner of the produce stall could be "pointing at the produce", and one in a park with a flying kite "maybe at the kite", so the pointing line now keeps clear of standing structures and kite strings and the storm never shares a picture with a flying kite; a kite string passed "very close to (possibly through)" a clothesline post; a girl reaching for the ball stood where it was "up and to the left of her, not directly above"; and a dog bowed toward the frame edge. Read again, the pointers were "warning that rain is coming" in all three storm pictures and both reaching children were under their ball ("seems to be reaching for it"). The kite was the one change still read two ways ("may be caught in the tree rather than flying freely"), so a twig now crosses it and a second leaf clump covers its lower corner; in the third round both readers put it in the tree ("stuck in its branches"; "it is clearly in the tree ... The string is slack and curved rather than tight").
intro: Four of the five templates that failed in v0.10 passed the eighth screen with full marks, each in three pictures: the waving man clear of the house read as "waving" every time, the kite in the tree was stuck in the branches every time, the child under the ball was "reaching for it", and the pointer at the storm clouds was "warning that rain is coming" in all three storm pictures. The set scored its best inference mean of the eight screens, 0.95, and its best overall mean, 0.99, with unintended oddities down to 1.0 per picture. The gate stays at 59 of 64: of the five that fail, four passed in v0.10, each lost points in one picture only, and two of them in the busiest picture of the set (`vision/flaws_v011.md`).
screen: Across all 61 pictures only 11 of 705 scored items fell short of full marks, and one was misread. Four of the 11, the misread among them, are in one picture, the busiest isomorph (23 items), where a small girl's kicking leg and yellow shoe read as "a wooden bat with a yellow end" and a digger with his head bowed "leans on the spade ... as if tired or unwell". In the set the inference points lost were that picture's trip, nobody predicting a fall, and the soaked package read as a badly aimed sprinkler. Unintended oddities fell from 1.5 to 1.0 per picture; none of the v0.10 oddities came back.
redrawn: Four of the five read with full marks. The play bow is the exception: it read in two pictures ("in a play bow (front legs down, rear up)") and failed again by one half point in the busiest park, front and centre, "in a stretch or play-bow pose", the same hedge as in v0.10.
gate: Every template was screened in at least three pictures (53 in three, 11 in four to six). Each of the five failures lost points in one picture only: a misread kick and a half-read dig in the busiest isomorph, the play bow in the busiest park, a floating box hanging low against the fence ("tipped over and resting at the foot of the fence"), and a square wheel read as "a separate box ... the real wheel hidden behind it". The retest of v0.9 put reader variance at about five templates, the size of this list; what changes from release to release is which templates fail and why.
